questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rare Eastern Imperial Eagle confirmed in Tamil Nadu in January 2026:
1. The Eastern Imperial Eagle (Aquila heliaca) is listed Vulnerable by the IUCN.
2. It was confirmed at Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, which lies at the tri-junction of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala.
3. Mudumalai Tiger Reserve is located in Kerala's Wayanad district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The eagle, a winter migrant, was confirmed at Mudumalai (321 sq km) in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu. The reserve is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve and sits where three States meet, but it is not in Wayanad.

questions.q:
Two Bactrian camels took part in the 2026 Republic Day parade. Consider the following statements:
1. The Bactrian camel has two humps.
2. A small population of about 300 to 400 Bactrian camels in India is found in the Nubra Valley of Ladakh.
3. The species is native to the hot deserts of the Thar and the Arabian Peninsula.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Bactrian camel (Camelus bactrianus) is a two-humped animal adapted to cold deserts, native to the steppes and deserts of Central Asia such as the Gobi and Taklamakan, which makes statement 3 wrong. In India it survives only in the Nubra Valley of Ladakh. The one-humped dromedary is the camel of hot Arabian deserts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian bison (gaur) in Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary, Odisha:
1. The population rose by 189 in a year to 848.
2. The gaur is listed Endangered by the IUCN.
3. The gaur is in CITES Appendix I and Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The count in Debrigarh, in Bargarh district near the Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi, grew about 28 per cent. The gaur is Vulnerable, not Endangered, on the IUCN Red List, though it has the highest legal protection (Schedule I) and CITES Appendix I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Galaxy Frog (Melanobatrachus indicus):
1. It is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
2. Seven individuals that disappeared in a recent study were lost to a fungal disease.
3. It is the flagship species of Mathikettan Shola National Park in Idukki.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The tiny frog (2 to 3.5 cm, IUCN Vulnerable) is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu and is the flagship species of Mathikettan Shola National Park. The seven missing frogs were blamed on unethical wildlife photography and photo tourism, not disease, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.q: Phayre's leaf monkey (Trachypithecus phayrei) was reported in January 2026 to be changing its behaviour because of habitat loss. Which one of the following is correct about the species?
o: It is listed Critically Endangered and found only in the Western Ghats
It is listed Vulnerable and found mainly in Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim
It is listed Least Concern and found across peninsular India
It is listed Endangered by the IUCN and found mainly in Tripura, Assam and Mizoram
questions.e: The primate occurs mainly in Tripura, Assam and Mizoram, eastern Bangladesh and western Myanmar, is Endangered on the IUCN list and appears in CITES Appendix II. The Western Ghats and peninsular options belong to other primates.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gegeneophis valmiki, described in January 2026:
1. It is a new caecilian from the Eastern Ghats of Odisha.
2. India has 42 caecilian species among its 457 amphibians.
3. The Western Ghats have 26 endemic caecilians, 11 of them in the genus Gegeneophis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Gegeneophis valmiki is a blind caecilian from the northern Western Ghats of Maharashtra, the first new addition to the genus in over a decade. Statement 1 gives the wrong region.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the second nationwide range-wide estimation of riverine and estuarine dolphins under Project Dolphin:
1. It was launched by the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
2. It estimates Irrawaddy dolphins in the Sundarbans and Odisha for the first time.
3. The Irrawaddy dolphin is an obligate freshwater species listed Endangered by the IUCN.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Irrawaddy dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris) is euryhaline, tolerating both fresh and salt water, and in India occurs mainly in Chilika Lake. It is Endangered, but it is not an obligate freshwater species. Project Dolphin Phase II was among five national projects launched in 2025.

questions.q: Endangered Indian Skimmers were sighted in January 2026 along a 60 km stretch of the Ganga after nearly 20 years, within the
o: Kashi Turtle Sanctuary in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh
Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary in Bhagalpur, Bihar
National Chambal Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh
Hastinapur Wildlife Sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh
questions.e: The Indian skimmer (Rynchops albicollis) is Endangered and a sign of healthy rivers; breeding colonies are on the Chambal, Ganga, Yamuna, Mahanadi and Son. The sighting was in Bihar's Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary; the Chambal is a known breeding area, but it was not the site of this sighting.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Amazonian stingless bees that gained legal rights in January 2026:
1. They became the first insect in the world granted legal rights.
2. The rights were granted by a national law of Brazil.
3. Human guardians can sue on their behalf.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Peruvian municipality of Satipo adopted the Declaration of Rights for Native Stingless Bees by ordinance, not Brazil by national law. The rights include existing and flourishing, with human guardians able to sue. The bees pollinate over 80 per cent of Amazonian flora.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the Valley of Flowers National Park, where a forest fire burned for five days in January 2026?
o: It was declared a national park in 2005 and inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1982
It lies in Pithoragarh district and was discovered by Frank Smythe in 1951
It forms a core zone of the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve and was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2005
It forms the buffer zone of the Corbett Tiger Reserve
questions.e: The park in Chamoli, Uttarakhand, was declared a national park in 1982 and inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2005; the two dates are swapped in one option. It forms a core zone of the Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve and was discovered in 1931 by Frank Smythe. Uttarakhand sought IAF help to douse the fire.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Assam completed an eviction drive in January 2026 clearing about 6,200 bighas of Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary and displacing 710 families.
Statement-II: Burhachapori Wildlife Sanctuary was notified as a buffer zone of Kaziranga Tiger Reserve in 2007.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, but the 2007 buffer-zone notification is background and does not by itself explain the eviction drive. The sanctuary in Sonitpur district, south of the Brahmaputra, forms the Laokhowa-Burhachapori ecosystem.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ratapani Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh:
1. It will be named after archaeologist Dr Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar.
2. It covers about 1,271 sq km of the Vindhya ranges in Raisen and Sehore districts.
3. It contains the Bhimbetka rock shelters, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Madhya Pradesh announced that Ratapani will be named after Padma Shri awardee Dr Wakankar, who is associated with the Bhimbetka rock shelters inside the reserve. The reserve covers about 1,271 sq km north of the Narmada. All three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aralam Butterfly Sanctuary in Kerala:
1. The Aralam Wildlife Sanctuary was renamed on 11 January 2026, making it the State's first butterfly sanctuary.
2. It lies in Kannur district and borders Karnataka's Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary.
3. It lies in Wayanad district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Aralam in Kannur district shares borders with Brahmagiri and Kottiyoor sanctuaries, and the Cheenkanni River flows through it. It has over 266 butterfly species, more than 80 per cent of Kerala's, and is a habitat of the Schedule I slender loris.

questions.q: Two new wetlands were added to India's Ramsar list in January 2026, taking the total to 98. Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Patna Bird Sanctuary : Patna district, Bihar
Chhari-Dhand Wetland Reserve : Thar Desert, Rajasthan
Patna Bird Sanctuary : Etah district, Uttar Pradesh
Chhari-Dhand Wetland Reserve : Rann of Kutch, Odisha
questions.e: Patna Bird Sanctuary, founded in 1991 in Etah district, is the smallest bird sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh, and has no link with Patna city. Chhari-Dhand lies on the edge of the Banni grasslands in Kutch, Gujarat, and is home to the Dalmatian pelican and Indian skimmer.

questions.q: The foundation stone of the Kaziranga Elevated Corridor was laid in January 2026. The elevated, wildlife-friendly section is
o: 86.675 km long, within the four-laning of a 34.5 km stretch of NH-715
34.5 km long, within the four-laning of NH-37 between Guwahati and Jorhat
21 km long, within the four-laning of the Kaliabor-Numaligarh stretch of NH-715
34.5 km long, within the four-laning of the 86.675 km Kaliabor-Numaligarh stretch of NH-715
questions.e: The corridor lets animals cross beneath the highway along 34.5 km of the 86.675 km Kaliabor-Numaligarh section of NH-715. Kaziranga, a World Heritage Site since 1985, has the world's largest population of one-horned rhinoceroses.

questions.q:
The Expert Appraisal Committee recommended a major design overhaul of the proposed International Dugong Conservation Centre at Manora, Thanjavur. Consider the following statements:
1. The site lies in a CRZ-III No Development Zone and overlaps mangroves and seagrass.
2. The dugong is listed Endangered by the IUCN.
3. The dugong is in CITES Appendix I and Schedule I of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The committee objected to the CRZ-III No Development Zone location, mangroves and seagrass. The dugong is Vulnerable on the IUCN list, not Endangered. The Gulf of Mannar and Palk Bay seagrass meadows host over 13 species.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the All-India Tiger Estimation 2026:
1. Its first phase began at Thanthai Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary in Erode district, Tamil Nadu.
2. It is the sixth cycle and is conducted every two years.
3. Field staff use the M-STrIPES app, launched in 2010 by the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The estimation is the sixth cycle, held every four years (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022 earlier), so the two-year interval in statement 2 is wrong. The M-STrIPES app is used for patrol and census data.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists:
1. The UN General Assembly declared 2026 as the Year, with UNEP leading.
2. Grasslands cover about 24 per cent of India's area, with less than 1 per cent under formal conservation.
3. Banni Grassland in Kutch, Gujarat is described as Asia's largest.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Food and Agriculture Organization leads the International Year, not UNEP, so statement 1 is wrong. The other two are correct.

questions.q:
Ecologist Madhav Gadgil, who died in January 2026, chaired the Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (WGEEP). Consider the following statements:
1. The WGEEP was set up by the Environment Ministry in 2010.
2. It recommended declaring the entire Western Ghats an Ecologically Sensitive Area in three zones.
3. The Government adopted the Gadgil report's zoning in full.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Government instead followed the Kasturirangan High-Level Working Group (2013), which proposed 56,825 sq km as eco-sensitive. Gadgil's 2011 report was far wider in scope. He also founded the Centre for Ecological Sciences at IISc in 1982.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements from the MoEFCC Year-End Review 2025:
1. India added 11 Ramsar Sites in 2025, reaching 96, the highest in Asia.
2. Bhopal and Indore became India's first Ramsar Wetland Cities.
3. India has 30 cheetahs, including 19 born in India.
4. India has 33 Elephant Reserves.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Udaipur and Indore, not Bhopal, became the first Ramsar Wetland Cities. The review also reported Project Cheetah expanding to Gandhisagar Wildlife Sanctuary and 1,134 Protected Areas, so three statements are correct.

questions.q: Kerala officially declared Bacillus subtilis its State microbe in January 2026. Bacillus subtilis is
o: a Gram-negative bacterium that causes enteric fever
a filamentous fungus used to make antibiotics
a virus used to control insect pests
a spore-forming, Gram-positive probiotic bacterium found in soil and the human gut and used as a fungicide and crop-protection agent
questions.e: Bacillus subtilis is a spore-forming, Gram-positive bacterium that lives in soil and the gut and is used as a probiotic and in crop protection. It is neither pathogenic like the enteric fever bacterium nor a fungus or virus.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026:
1. They were notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and supersede the 2016 Rules.
2. They require three-stream segregation at source.
3. They introduce Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility and environmental compensation for non-compliance.
4. They take effect on 1 April 2026.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules require four-stream segregation (wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste), not three. They also raise RDF use by cement and waste-to-energy plants from 5 to 15 per cent over six years. Three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs):
1. The 2023 South Lhonak lake GLOF in Sikkim destroyed the Teesta III dam at Chungthang.
2. Glacial lakes across High Mountain Asia are shrinking, according to a study by IIT Roorkee.
3. The National GLOF Risk Mitigation Project covers Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The IIT Roorkee study found more than 31,000 glacial lakes growing across High Mountain Asia, with their area up 5.5 per cent, so statement 2 is wrong. South Lhonak (2023) wrecked the Teesta III dam, and the national GLOF mitigation project targets four Himalayan States. The Central Water Commission monitors over 900 glacial lakes.

questions.q: The Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target (Amendment) Rules, 2025 widened the obligated sectors under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme. Which one of the following lists the four sectors newly added?
o: Aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper
Iron and steel, thermal power, fertilisers and aviation
Petroleum refinery, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium
questions.e: Aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali and pulp and paper were the original obligated sectors; refineries, petrochemicals, textiles and secondary aluminium were added. 208 units must cut emission intensity by 3 to 7 per cent by 2026-27 against a 2023-24 baseline, buying Carbon Credit Certificates for any shortfall. Failure attracts environmental compensation of twice the average CCC price. The rules are under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

questions.q:
The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entered its definitive phase on 1 January 2026. Consider the following statements:
1. It imposes a carbon-related levy on imports of certain carbon-intensive goods.
2. Covered goods include iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, hydrogen and electricity.
3. It is meant to encourage firms to shift production to countries with weaker climate rules.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: CBAM, first applied in 2023 as a reporting-only transition, became a real levy from January 2026. It exists to prevent carbon leakage, the opposite of statement 3. Indian steel, aluminium and cement exports to the EU face higher costs, which is why India sought safeguards in its EU trade deal.
